Lead.title: Lead
Lead.description: Represents a potential customer (lead) captured through a landing page form.

formId.description: Reference to the LandingPageForm that the lead originated from. (Relationship: LandingPageForm 1:N Lead)

notes.description: Any additional notes about the lead.

dateCreated.description: The date and time when the lead was created.

LandingPageForm.title: LandingPageForm
LandingPageForm.description: Represents a form used on a landing page to capture leads.

id.description: Unique identifier for the landing page form.

name.description: The name of the landing page form (e.g., 'VSL Opt-in Form', 'Personalized Demo Form').

landingPageType.description: The type of landing page this form is associated with (e.g., 'VSL', 'Demo', 'Lead Magnet').

fields.description: A list of the fields included in the form (e.g. name, email, phone).

dateCreated.description: The date and time when the landing page form was created.

definition.description: Stores the configurations for various landing page forms. Includes metadata about the form's purpose and fields.

params.name: formId
params.description: The unique identifier for the landing page form.

definition.description: Stores lead data captured from landing page forms. Each document represents a single lead submission.

params.name: leadId
params.description: The unique identifier for the lead.

firestore.reasoning:
To effectively manage landing pages and capture leads for SORO™, the recommended Firestore structure focuses on clear organization and easy querying.  The structure leverages the `LandingPageForm` and `Lead` entities.  Each landing page will have its own form, and each submission of that form will create a `Lead` document. This design ensures that leads are directly associated with the landing page they originated from.

**Authorization Independence**: Authorization Independence is achieved by design, using the implicit ownership of documents within collections. There is no authorization logic specified in the user request; if authorization is required in the future (e.g. a user can only view leads submitted to *their* forms), denormalization may be required, such as by adding an `ownerId` field to the `Lead` documents, copying it from the `LandingPageForm`.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters)**: The design naturally supports secure `list` operations. List operations on `/leads` are possible without relying on filtering based on document content, as all documents in the `leads` collection will share the same security posture. If more complex access control is required, Structural Segregation can be applied. For instance, one could introduce an `adminLeads` collection with stricter access rules. With path-based ownership as described in the Authorization Independence section, rules can be applied such that a `User` can only view `/users/{userId}/leads`.
